title: When the Orchard Wakes
premise: In 1923, Ada Eriksen tends the apple orchard her family abandoned after the Great War, keeping her wartime ledger of forgotten names hidden beneath the floorboards. When Tomas Lindqvist arrives with a letter in the handwriting of Henrik Dahl—Ada's lost love, officially dead at Ypres—she learns Henrik survived, was repatriated to the wrong side of a redrawn border, and is now classified as an enemy alien awaiting deportation. To honor the promise she made him in a hospital garden in 1919—that if he ever reached for her, she would answer—Ada must smuggle Henrik's message past the authorities and reach the ship before it sails on the morning tide. She chooses exposure over safety, surrendering her ledger to the magistrate as evidence of Henrik's innocence, and the novel ends with Ada and Henrik planting a graft from the old orchard in a new country, the ledger finally read aloud.
about_author: Bram Vasquez is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing Red Cross prisoner-of-war records across Northern Europe. Their fiction has appeared in several literary journals, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Autumn pruning in the derelict orchard; Ada recalls her nursing years and the names she recorded that officers omitted. She checks the hidden ledger, a ritual of grief. Emotional beat: quiet, controlled loneliness—the safety of invisibility established before it is threatened.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Tomas Lindqvist arrives soaked from the road, carrying a letter in handwriting Ada knows better than her own—Henrik Dahl's, a man officially dead since 1917. Tomas claims to be a courier paid in Copenhagen. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past breaking through the floorboards.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback woven in. The letter reveals Henrik survived, was repatriated across the new border, and is now detained as an enemy alien awaiting deportation on a ship sailing in eleven days. Ada relives the hospital garden promise of 1919. Emotional beat: hope curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas observes the village's hostility toward anything foreign, and Ada's careful reputation. He withholds that he was paid by someone else—Henrik's sister. Emotional beat: unease; the reader senses Tomas is not what he seems.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada maps the impossible logistics: the port, the magistrate, the ship's schedule. She tests the village's loyalties with small questions and gets silence in return. Emotional beat: the planner at war with her own caution.

chapters.title: The Sister's Money
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas confesses to himself that he kept part of Ingrid Dahl's payment and intends to keep more; he has his own brother on that deportation list. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into a private, parallel mission.

chapters.title: Grafts and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. While grafting apple stock, Ada remembers Henrik teaching her the craft before the war, and the promise: 'If I ever reach for you, answer.' She cuts a scion from the oldest tree to carry with her. Emotional beat: tenderness as fuel for resolve.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Tea
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada visits Magistrate Holm under a pretext and realizes he already knows a letter has circulated—the border authorities flagged it. Holm is not a villain but a tired man enforcing rules he half despises. Emotional beat: the trap tightening without malice.

chapters.title: Tomas Taken
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Authorities detain Tomas at the inn, finding Ingrid's remaining payment; he is questioned about the letter's origin. He refuses to name Ada. Emotional beat: an opportunist discovering he has, without meaning to, become loyal.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Weight
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reads her ledger by lamplight, deciding whether it can serve as evidence of Henrik's identity and conduct—names, dates, testimonies of the men who owed him their lives. Emotional beat: the choice between her archive of the invisible and her living promise.

chapters.title: Ingrid's Second Letter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A second letter from Ingrid Dahl arrives, revealing Tomas was meant to bring money for a lawyer, not merely a message—and that Henrik refuses to board the ship without knowing whether Ada answered. Emotional beat: the promise made mutual; stakes become personal on both ends.

chapters.title: What Silences Cost
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, from detention. Tomas trades information with a sympathetic guard to warn Ada that the ship's departure moved up two days. Emotional beat: sacrifice by a man who never planned to sacrifice anything.

chapters.title: The Warning in the Rain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The guard's note reaches Ada through the orchard gate. Two days gone. She begins moving at night: copying the ledger, hiding the original, packing the scion. Emotional beat: adrenaline under stillness; the invisible woman learning to move visibly.

chapters.title: Holm's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ada and Holm's shared scene, mostly Ada's POV. Ada offers the ledger openly if Holm will delay the deportation for a hearing; Holm admits he lacks the authority but knows a clerk who owes him. Emotional beat: an alliance built on shared weariness, not trust.

chapters.title: The Hearing That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The hearing is cancelled; the order comes from above. Holm is suspended. Ada realizes the system will not bend and that the only route left is the port itself. Emotional beat: despair converted into decision—the novel's hinge.

chapters.title: Night Roads
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada's and Tomas's POVs. Ada travels by cart and foot toward the port; Tomas, released on a technicality, follows the same roads, each unaware of the other. Emotional beat: two converging journeys, tension rising with every mile.

chapters.title: The Port at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reaches the harbor, finds the ship berthed early, and is refused at every checkpoint. She watches the gangway and understands she cannot get aboard—only get Henrik's name spoken where it matters. Emotional beat: the planner out of plans.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax begins. On the quay, Ada publicly reads names from her ledger—men saved by Henrik Dahl—drawing a crowd, including a Red Cross delegate who once signed her pages. Emotional beat: the private archive becoming public testimony; her invisibility burned as fuel.

chapters.title: The Gangway
chapters.summary: Ada's and Henrik's shared scene. The delegate halts the boarding for verification; Henrik, hearing his own name in the crowd, reaches across the barrier—and Ada answers the twenty-year-old promise, taking his hand. Tomas arrives with Ingrid's lawyer's papers. Emotional beat: catharsis; the reach and the answer.

chapters.title: What the Morning Tide Took
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The ship sails with Henrik's name struck from the manifest pending review; Tomas parts from them at the quay, refusing reward, bound for his own brother's file. Emotional beat: bittersweet release; debts acknowledged, not all repaid.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Verdict
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, Holm, reinstated, rules the ledger admissible and Henrik's status revised. The village that stayed silent must now live beside the story it ignored; some doors open, some close forever. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, belonging renegotiated.

chapters.title: When the Orchard Wakes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue in spring. Ada and Henrik plant the scion from the old tree in new ground; she reads the ledger aloud once, then closes it for good—its names now carried by living people. Emotional beat: resolution; memory inherited rather than hidden, belonging chosen rather than granted.
